lane: FTREE (lane 26): architecture-specific failure trees, track 2 (architecture comparison preparation)
scope: Ways each candidate thrust architecture (hall_only, rf_hall, ecr_hall) could fail the programme against the RFP hard gates (CLAUDE.md RFP envelope: 180-230 km, 12-25 mN, < 1.5 kW, < 40 kg, 26,000 h mission, > 15,000 h firing, air + Xe). no_winner_statement: This file declares no winner and eliminates no architecture. Every node is decision_state 'open'. Evidence status describes whether published evidence makes a failure path credible; it is not a verdict on any Vyovrinda design. The ranking orders evidence to acquire, not architectures.

failure_classes.name: ignition
failure_classes.description: The discharge (or pre-ionizer) does not start on the delivered feed without an allowed aid.

failure_classes.name: sustainment_extinction
failure_classes.description: The discharge extinguishes, oscillates destructively or leaves its operating window over the delivered feed envelope.

failure_classes.name: utilization
failure_classes.description: Too little of the atmospheric feed is ionized and accelerated to meet thrust within bus power; for two-stage arms, the pre-ionizer does not pay for itself.

failure_classes.name: cathode_limit
failure_classes.description: Cathode current, flow (Xe inventory), poisoning or life limits the programme.

failure_classes.name: thermal_limit
failure_classes.description: A component exceeds its temperature limit (Hall magnets and walls; RF coil/coupler; ECR magnets/resonator).

failure_classes.name: erosion_wall_life
failure_classes.description: Erosion, oxidation or coating of plasma-facing parts limits firing life.

failure_classes.name: power_limit
failure_classes.description: The bus-power gate cannot be met at the thrust gate.

failure_classes.name: mass_limit
failure_classes.description: The mass gate cannot be met (hardware plus Xe inventory).

failure_classes.name: control_startup
failure_classes.description: Start, restart or the Xe -> mixed -> atmosphere transition cannot be controlled.

failure_classes.name: interstage_loss
failure_classes.description: Ions made in the pre-ionizer are lost before the Hall acceleration zone, or the stages couple unstably.

failure_classes.name: rf_source_specific
failure_classes.description: RF-source-specific modes: E-H (capacitive-inductive) transition and hysteresis, impedance matching, magnetized-source field interaction, RF interference.

failure_classes.name: ecr_source_specific
failure_classes.description: ECR-specific modes: cutoff/overdense limit, interaction between ECR and Hall magnetic fields, microwave power chain.

evidence_status_rule.meaning: evidence_status says whether open-literature evidence makes the failure mechanism credible (physically operative in a relevant device or regime). It is not a gate verdict for a Vyovrinda design; that is decision_state, which is 'open' for every node in v1.

directions.supports: the source shows or states that the mechanism occurs (or limited a relevant device) in its domain
directions.contradicts: the source shows the mechanism did not occur, or was avoided, in a relevant device within its domain
directions.context: relevant but not decisive in either direction (different regime, design intent, mitigation validated only on another propellant, cause not attributed, or evidence that covers only some legs of a failure path stated as a disjunction, e.g. N-RF-02: a mismatch at ignition, at the Xe <-> air change or across the flow envelope)

rule: supported: at least one 'supports' item and no 'contradicts' item
contradicted: at least one 'contradicts' item and no 'supports' item
unknown: no 'supports' and no 'contradicts' item (no evidence, or context only), or both present (conflicting)

unknown_basis.conflicting: both supporting and contradicting items exist; applicability decides and is not yet established
unknown_basis.no_evidence: no applicable open-literature item was found; evidence_gap says what is missing

evidence_status_rule.gas_rule: Every evidence item on an air_specific node declares the gas of the cited result: gas_stated (the gas the source states, which must appear in the item's statement or applicability) or gas_not_stated = true. A gas_not_stated item is context on an air_specific node whatever it reports. A decisive item (supports / contradicts) must carry gas_stated; if that gas contains no atmospheric species (N2, O2, O, N, air), the item must also carry gas_independent_rationale saying why the mechanism does not depend on the gas (e.g. the cutoff density n_c(f) depends only on frequency).

elimination_rule.text: An architecture is eliminated only through explicit hard-gate logic: a node linked to a hard gate moves to resolved_fail for that architecture, and the supporting evidence is either (a) a measurement on Vyovrinda hardware or essentially identical hardware (EVIDENCE.md levels 1-2, quantity type measured) at the relevant operating condition, or (b) a physics bound that holds for every design of that architecture family independently of any Hall transport closure. Literature on other devices (level >= 3), screening candidates and unadmitted closures never eliminate. Proposed for the owner; not applied in v1 (eliminations = []).

action_effects.decides: The action's output alone settles the node, given only owner-fixed inputs (thresholds, margins, allocations, allowed Xe roles, operations-concept assumptions) and design-fixed inputs (component ratings and datasheet limits). If decision_quantity.requires_actions names another action, this action cannot decide the node.
action_effects.contributes: The action's output is a necessary member of the jointly sufficient set named in cheapest_resolution (or of another jointly sufficient set of the node's contributing actions); it is not sufficient alone.
action_effects.informs: The action narrows, prioritises or cross-checks the node but is not needed to settle it (for example a literature search, an unvalidated model, or a blocked Hall-map analysis).
action_effects.rule: decision_quantity.requires_actions lists every action whose output the threshold comparison needs. Each listed action is 'contributes' on the node (or is the single deciding action), no other action may 'decide' it, and every listed action is in cheapest_resolution.

node_rules.sub_cause_rule: A node whose threshold is its parent's threshold comparison (the same inequality, possibly restated on an intermediate quantity whose required value follows only from the parent's threshold) is a sub-cause: sub_cause_of names the parent, it takes the parent's comparison_id, gates, requires_actions, cheapest_resolution and deciding/contributing actions, its threshold names the parent, and it is not counted in the ranking. A node whose threshold has its own basis (a physics bound, a component rating or datasheet limit, a design tolerance, an owner allocation, or its own RFP number) is counted.
node_rules.comparison_rule: decision_quantity.comparison_id names the threshold comparison. Counted nodes of one architecture (core plus any one choice of design-branch options) never share a comparison_id or a threshold text; a sub-cause shares its parent's comparison_id.
node_rules.gate_link_rule: A node links the hard gates whose criterion fails directly when its threshold is not met (hard_gates[].links_when says what each link means). Costs of mitigating a failure (the power or mass of cooling, shielding or margins) are booked in N-PWR-01 and N-MAS-01 and are not linked from the node that causes them.
node_rules.delivered_feed_rule: A node whose decision quantity or threshold is evaluated on the delivered feed (its state, composition, pressure or flow envelope at IF-A5, including the atmospheric end state of a transition) needs that feed from A-FLOWENV, so A-FLOWENV is in requires_actions (or decides the node). A node evaluated at a design setpoint (discharge power, flow and magnet setting fixed by the design, e.g. the thermal nodes) takes the setpoint as a design input.
node_rules.cheapest_resolution_rule: cheapest_resolution is the minimum, over the unblocked single deciding actions, cheapest_resolution itself and any alternative_resolutions (other jointly sufficient sets of contributing actions), of the key (highest cost class in the set, number of actions, sorted action ids). Every contributing action belongs to cheapest_resolution or to one alternative_resolutions set.
node_rules.physical_cause_basis: physical_cause_basis says what carries the physical cause: 'cited' (it names the source or derived-value ids that state it), 'definition' (a ledger or budget identity, no physics claim) or 'hypothesis' (the failure hypothesis, marked 'verify').

nodes.title: Hall-stage cold start on atmospheric anode flow fails; start needs Xe
nodes.mechanism: Breakdown and transition to a self-sustained Hall discharge need enough neutral density and seed electrons in the channel; N2/O2 at ABEP-delivered density may not start without a noble-gas start.
nodes.physical_cause: Channel neutral density set by the intake rather than a flow controller, one to two orders of magnitude below standard Hall thrusters in the RAM-HET design estimate (S-ANDREUSSI2017); the higher ionization and inelastic (vibrational, dissociation) energy cost of N2/O2 than Xe is not quantified by a cited item here - verify.

evidence.statement: 'The PPS1350-TSD was always ignited with xenon. After ignition, a smooth transition from 100% xenon to 100% nitrogen or N2/O2 mixture at the anode was carried out; the cathode continued to work with xenon.'
evidence.applicability: Test procedure on a 1.4 kW-limited laboratory Hall thruster; air-only ignition was not reported as attempted.
evidence.gas_stated: xenon (ignition, cathode); N2 or N2/O2 mixture (anode after transition)

evidence.statement: The integrated RAM-EP system 'was successfully ignited with the atmospheric propellant provided by the PFG (operating at 4.7 mg/s mass flow rate of pure N2-O2)'; the intake let the RAM-HET 'ignite a pure N2-O2 flow at an acceleration voltage equal to 300 V and an ionization voltage equal to 100 V'.
evidence.applicability: Double-stage Hall thruster in a ground facility with a Xe-fed cathode (cathode ignition with xenon, Sec. III.F); not a single-stage Hall and not flight density.

evidence.statement: 'HET ignitions and stable operation are achieved when the neutral gas density is sufficiently high'; 'In a RAM-EP system, the properties of the neutral flow inside the thruster channel critically depends on the intake configuration and on the atmospheric conditions outside of the system'; estimated thruster-inlet neutral density 1e17-1e18 m^-3, 'from one to two orders of magnitude' below the ionization region of standard HETs.
evidence.applicability: Source's design estimate for its intake; the Vyovrinda delivered density is set by the upstream chain (A-FLOWENV).

evidence.statement: 'the thruster unit needs further optimization to operate on atmospheric propellant ... In particular, the RAM-HET also requires injection of Xe to aid the ignition of the thruster, as well as to operate the neutraliser' (citing the SITAEL RAM-EP papers).
evidence.applicability: Secondary statement about the SITAEL RAM-HET.

decision_quantity.quantity: Start success per attempt on atmospheric-only anode flow at the delivered feed state (IF-A5); Xe used per start when a Xe start is used
decision_quantity.threshold: Every start the operations concept needs (N_start) succeeds on the delivered atmospheric feed without Xe, or with a Xe per start that the air_xe rules allow; the start Xe for N_start is within the Xe loaded for starts, so it is not depleted before the end of the mission (TBD - requires the owner's restart count, allowed Xe roles and Xe allocation)
decision_quantity.requires: restart count (A-OPS, from owner assumptions); delivered feed state (A-FLOWENV); allowed Xe roles (air_xe gate TBD); Xe allocation (owner)
requires_owner_inputs: operations-concept assumptions for the restart count

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Demonstrate Hall-stage start on the delivered atmospheric feed state, or a Xe-assisted start whose Xe per start the air_xe rules allow and whose start Xe over the mission fits the Xe loaded for starts.

nodes.title: RF pre-ionizer does not break down on N2/O2 at the delivered pressure
nodes.mechanism: Inductive/helicon breakdown on molecular gases at low pressure needs higher fields than on noble gases; the source may need a noble-gas start.
nodes.physical_cause: Harder breakdown on N2/O2 than on argon or xenon, observed in an RF ion thruster (S-CIFALI2011); the attribution to higher ionization energy and electron energy losses of N2/O2 is not quantified by a cited item - verify.

evidence.statement: RIT-10 EBB: 'The argon is used to ignite the thruster, as the ignition with N2/O2 was found to be much more difficult ... xenon ignites even better than argon.'
evidence.applicability: RF (inductive) ion thruster discharge chamber, Giessen facility; a gridded RF discharge, not an RF pre-ionizer feeding a Hall stage.

evidence.statement: A frequency 'equal or higher than 27.12 MHz' was chosen 'as it leads to easier ignition at low pressure' (from literature and preliminary numerics).
evidence.applicability: Design guidance for an inductive plasma thruster, not a measurement; no gas stated for this guidance.

decision_quantity.requires: delivered pressure (A-FLOWENV) and allowed Xe roles

nodes.title: ECR pre-ionizer does not break down on air at the delivered pressure
nodes.mechanism: Microwave/ECR breakdown needs the resonance condition inside the source and enough neutral density for the electron energy gain to produce ionization.
nodes.physical_cause: Resonance field, wave coupling and electron energy losses on N2/O2 (hypothesis; no item that states the gas shows ECR breakdown behaviour on air - verify).

evidence.statement: Abstract: 'experimental demonstration of plasma ignition in an electron-cyclotron-resonance atmosphere-breathing electric propulsion source at pressures representative of very low Earth orbit' and 'sustained plasma discharge at pressures consistent with conditions expected after intake compression at altitudes near 200 km'.
evidence.applicability: Laboratory ECR ABEP source with a MHz-range birdcage resonator. The abstract (re-read via Crossref 2026-09-26) does not state the gas, so air or N2/O2 breakdown is not established; not decisive until the full text (L-ECRHALL) gives the composition.

evidence.statement: Microwave cathode: 'Plasma formation was very reliable and never required the use of any separate ignition' (xenon and argon).
evidence.applicability: Noble gases only; nitrogen-oxygen not attempted (Sec. V).

nodes.title: Pre-ionizer seed plasma does not lower the Hall-stage start requirement
nodes.mechanism: The two-stage start benefit (seed plasma from the pre-ionizer triggering the Hall discharge at lower feed density) may not materialize if the seed does not reach the Hall channel.
nodes.physical_cause: Interstage loss of seed charge and field-line connection between the stages (hypothesis; no item measures the seed effect of an RF or ECR stage on a Hall start - verify).

evidence.statement: Double-stage RAM-HET: 'the first stage showed a good capability to ionize the flow provided by the PFG' (the PFG supplied a pure N2-O2 flow, abstract).
evidence.applicability: DC magnetic-confinement first stage, not RF or ECR; does not isolate the start threshold.

nodes.title: Hall stage extinguishes or runs unstably on N2/O2 within the needed window
nodes.mechanism: The sustained operating window (voltage, flow, magnetic field) on molecular propellant is narrow; outside it the discharge extinguishes or enters strongly oscillating modes.
nodes.physical_cause: Ionization balance of N2/O2 at channel density and mode changes with the magnetic-field setting (sustainment limits on N2 in S-BRABSTON2025 and S-MARCHIONI2020).

evidence.statement: P5 on N2: the text states the discharge cannot be sustained above 275 V or below 225 V; all five setpoints N1-N5 ran (repo audit finding F4 reads 275 V as an approximate boundary).
evidence.locator: Repo audit p5_n2_measurement_audit_findings_v1.json: admissible_targets.sustained_discharge, finding F4
evidence.applicability: 5-kW-class P5, 5.0-5.4 mg/s N2 anode, Xe cathode, facility pressure 1.1-2.1e-5 Torr.

evidence.statement: ECHT on N2: 3 of 7 thrust runs flagged strongly unstable; the thruster changed modes during calibration.
evidence.applicability: ECHT, 2.06 mg/s N2, 180-220 V, facility pressure 0.8-2.5e-4 Torr, argon cathode.

evidence.statement: PPS1350-TSD on 1.27N2+O2: 'Stable operation occurs with a mass flow rate as low as 2.1 mg/s' and 'The thruster has operated stably during the 10 hours test.'
evidence.applicability: Laboratory Hall thruster, Xe cathode, Xe start, 10-h firing.

evidence.statement: RAM-HET standalone: 'Attempts to operate the thruster with N2-O2 mixture were performed but a certain amount of xenon (~1.5 mg/s) has always been necessary to prevent the flame out'.
evidence.applicability: Double-stage RAM-HET in standalone configuration.

nodes.title: Delivered-flow range over altitude and solar activity exceeds the sustainment range
nodes.mechanism: The intake-delivered flow varies with altitude (180-230 km) and solar activity; if the ratio of maximum to minimum delivered flow is larger than the flow range over which the discharge is sustained, throttling fails at one end.
nodes.physical_cause: Atmospheric density variability transmitted through the intake/compressor chain to the thruster interface (the channel flow depends on intake and atmospheric conditions, S-ANDREUSSI2017; the Vyovrinda variation comes from the frozen atmosphere through A-FLOWENV).

evidence.statement: 'In a RAM-EP system, the properties of the neutral flow inside the thruster channel critically depends on the intake configuration and on the atmospheric conditions outside of the system.'
evidence.applicability: General statement by an ABEP developer that the channel neutral flow varies with intake and atmospheric conditions. It does not compare a delivered-flow envelope with a sustained flow range, so it is context; the Vyovrinda envelope comes from A-FLOWENV and the sustained range from M-SUSWIN.

decision_quantity.requires: A-FLOWENV (upstream, Hall-independent) and M-SUSWIN

nodes.title: Two-stage coupling: excess acceleration-stage current or unstable interaction limits the Hall stage
nodes.mechanism: With a separate ionization stage, electron current into the acceleration stage and the interaction of the two discharges can cap the usable acceleration voltage or destabilize operation.
nodes.physical_cause: Electron supply and potential distribution between the stages and power-supply coupling, shown for a DC first stage (S-ANDREUSSI2017); for an RF or ECR first stage it is a hypothesis - verify.

evidence.statement: 'the current circulating in the acceleration stage was always significantly higher than expected. This phenomenon posed a limit to the applicable acceleration voltage and, in turn, to the achievable thrust'; in standalone Xe tests both supplies went to current limitation and both voltages dropped to around 100 V.
evidence.locator: Sec. IV (pdf p. 10); Sec. III.E (pdf p. 7)
evidence.applicability: Double-stage Hall thruster whose first stage is a DC discharge, not an RF or ECR pre-ionizer; it shows two-stage coupling in a DC/DC device, so context for the rf_hall and ecr_hall coupling node.

nodes.title: Low ion utilization of N2/O2 in the Hall stage prevents 12 mN within the bus power
nodes.mechanism: A small ionized fraction of the atmospheric feed (and beam divergence) gives low thrust per unit flow and per unit power.
nodes.physical_cause: Energy sinks of molecular gases (vibrational excitation, dissociation) and low channel neutral density at ABEP flows (lower ionisation efficiency on N2 than on Xe, S-CIFALI2011; N2 vibrational losses as the dominant electron energy loss in an N2-O2 helicon, S-WANG2026). nodes.title: E-H (or helicon) mode transition with hysteresis drops the RF stage to a low-density mode
nodes.mechanism: Inductive sources have a weak capacitive E mode and a dense inductive H mode; the E->H transition occurs at a higher coil current than H->E, so a power, flow or composition change can drop the source to E mode and recovery needs more power.
nodes.physical_cause: Nonlinear electron power balance giving hysteresis (S-TURNER1999, gas not stated); composition-dependent transition power in N2-O2 (S-WANG2026) and mode changes with the N2-Ar ratio (S-ZHANG2024).

evidence.statement: Abstract: 'The E-to-H transition occurs at a larger coil current than the H-to-E transition, and a range of currents between these values supports either E or H mode. This effect is called hysteresis', attributed to nonlinear effects in the electron power balance.
evidence.applicability: General inductive-discharge physics (the abstract refers to discharges used for plasma processing) with no gas stated, so context on this air-specific node; S-WANG2026 (N2-O2) and S-ZHANG2024 (N2-Ar) carry the node.

evidence.statement: Abstract: with N2:O2 from 1:4 to 4:1, 'mode transition power exhibits notable reduction at N2:O2 = 1:4'; N2:O2 of about 2:3 is a transition region between O2- and N2-dominated behaviour.
evidence.applicability: Helicon plasma for air-breathing thrusters; transition power depends on composition.

evidence.statement: Abstract: plasma morphology, emission spectrum and spatial profile 'change significantly during mode transitions with the N2-Ar ratio'.
evidence.applicability: N2-Ar helicon plasma at fixed power and field.

nodes.title: Cutoff (overdense) limit: ECR-stage density saturates below the Hall-stage feed need
nodes.mechanism: Microwaves launched from the low-field side are reflected where the plasma frequency exceeds the wave frequency (O-mode cutoff n_c(f); the X-mode R-cutoff lies at lower density), capping density unless another wave mode or launch is used.
nodes.physical_cause: n_c(f) = epsilon_0 m_e (2 pi f)^2 / e^2 (derived values D-ECR-NC-2.45GHZ, D-ECR-NC-5.8GHZ, D-ECR-NC-5.85GHZ).

evidence.statement: At 2.45 GHz and 750 W the measured near-grid density 'was as high as 6x10^10 #/cm3, very close to the cutoff density at this frequency'; the second-generation engine moved to 5.85 GHz; above cutoff 'the microwaves are no longer absorbed, but reflected to regions of lower field strength'. The same report attributes a later density saturation near the ion grid more likely to high utilization than to cutoff ('The high calculated grid currents suggest that the latter possibility likely prevails').
evidence.locator: Sections 'Basic Design and Discharge Performance Implications' (pdf p. 8) and 'Early Microwave Ion Source Development' (pdf p. 11); section 'Plasma density' of the discharge results (pdf p. 21)
evidence.applicability: HiPEP ECR ion-thruster discharge on xenon.
evidence.gas_independent_rationale: The O-mode cutoff density n_c(f) = epsilon_0 m_e (2 pi f)^2 / e^2 depends only on the wave frequency, not on the gas, so a density at or above n_c at the source's frequency bears on the cutoff mechanism for any gas; whether an air-fed stage needs a density above n_c is not shown.

evidence.statement: Estimated cavity plasma densities 1e18-1e19 m^-3 (xenon) and 6e17-3e18 m^-3 (argon) exceed the stated 'critical density at 5.8 GHz = 4x10^17 m^-3'.
evidence.applicability: Microwave cathode; densities inferred from an ion-migration current limit, not measured.
evidence.gas_independent_rationale: The O-mode cutoff density n_c(f) = epsilon_0 m_e (2 pi f)^2 / e^2 depends only on the wave frequency, not on the gas, so a density at or above n_c at the source's frequency bears on the cutoff mechanism for any gas; whether an air-fed stage needs a density above n_c is not shown. Whether a microwave discharge runs above n_c is a matter of wave coupling and launch, which the node's threshold admits as a demonstrated overdense route; the densities here are inferred with noble-gas ion properties, so air is not shown.

evidence.statement: Cut-off density at 2.45 GHz is 7.4e16 m^-3; 'the electron density observed in microwave cathodes is significantly higher than nc', so microwaves do not penetrate the overdense bulk and heating occurs near the antenna.
evidence.applicability: A general statement about microwave cathodes that states no gas for the densities it refers to, so context on this air-specific node; applicability to an ion-producing pre-ionizer is not shown either.

nodes.title: ECR resonance field interacts with the Hall magnetic circuit
nodes.mechanism: The resonance surface needs |B| = 2 pi f m_e / e near the source while the Hall channel needs its own B(z); the ECR magnets distort the Hall topology and the Hall circuit (and its current schedule between Xe and air setpoints) moves the resonance surface.
nodes.physical_cause: The resonance field scales with frequency, |B| = 2 pi f m_e / e (35.7 G per 100 MHz, derived D-ECR-B-PER-100MHZ). At GHz frequencies it is several times the peak radial field of a Hall channel such as P5 (130-162.5 G): 0.0875 T at 2.45 GHz (derived), so the ECR magnets are the stronger field and can distort the Hall topology. A MHz-range source (S-STASTNY2026) needs a resonance field of the order of, or below, Hall-channel fields; there the Hall circuit's stray field can itself set or move the resonance surface. Either way the two fields interact; which one dominates depends on the chosen frequency.

evidence.statement: 'For f = 2.45 GHz, the corresponding ECR magnetic-field strength BECR is 87.5 mT.'
evidence.applicability: Physics statement; reproduced by D-ECR-B-2.45GHZ.

evidence.statement: P5 peak radial B 162.5 G at the Xe setpoints and 130 G at the N2 setpoints; coils tuned at N3 and held.
evidence.locator: hallthruster_bridge/cases/p5_xenon.json source field (Table 4); p5_n2_measurement_audit_findings_v1.json finding F6

evidence.applicability: General statement.

evidence.applicability: A lower resonance frequency lowers the required field; route relevant to the interaction, not a demonstration with a Hall circuit.

nodes.title: Emitter poisoning by oxygen from the feed, plume backflow or ram exposure
nodes.condition: Applies only if the cathode has a thermionic emitter, i.e. on the Xe-fed hollow-cathode branch (design_branches cathode_feed = xe_fed_thermionic).
nodes.mechanism: Oxygen on the thermionic emitter raises the work function, cutting emission and destabilizing the cathode (plume mode), with erosion at high temperature.
nodes.physical_cause: Surface chemistry of BaO-W and LaB6 emitters in oxidizing environments (poisoning at minimal air pressure, S-TISAEV2023A, a secondary statement).

evidence.statement: 'exposure of the emitter materials, such as barium-oxide impregnated tungsten (BaO-W) or lanthanum-hexaboride (LaB6), to oxygen results in poisoning of the material surface and prompts a significant decrease in the current density at even minimal values of air pressure'; operation of a LaB6 hollow cathode on xenon containing a 12% fraction of a 0.48O2 + 0.52N2 mixture 'results in significant erosion of the emitter and cathode structure' (citing refs [9, 10] and [1] = S-ANDREUSSI2022).
evidence.applicability: Secondary statements; primary sources not read (S-ANDREUSSI2022 targeted by L-CATHODE).

evidence.statement: Abstract: on an unused segmented LaB6 emitter the plume-mode region expanded during a discharge experiment; the surface showed 'oxygen and carbon detection', but 'the dominant substance in the region where carbon is detected was lanthanum carbide', where 'an increase in the work function is indicated', which 'appears to increase the plasma instability'; plume mode 'severely degrades the overall cathode lifetime'.
evidence.applicability: Laboratory LaB6 hollow cathode; the work-function rise is attributed mainly to carbon (lanthanum carbide), oxygen is only detected, and the contamination source is not an air feed. Weak for oxygen poisoning, so context only.

evidence.statement: ECHT tests ran a degraded BaO emitter cathode (IonTech HCN-252) on argon.
evidence.applicability: Degradation cause not attributed.

evidence.statement: After two days of RAM-HET Xe / N2-O2 testing 'cathode ignition could not be achieved anymore'; inspection showed 'a damaged emitter'.
evidence.applicability: Cause not attributed by the source.

evidence.statement: 'Use of a thermionic hollow cathode, perhaps with a relatively oxygen-tolerant LaB6 insert, coupled with a small on-board supply of xenon may be an adequate solution'; for long missions the author assumes hot parts exposed to the oxidizing environment should be avoided.
evidence.applicability: Design judgement citing S-GOEBEL2007.

evidence.statement: 'The second test was an 1800-hour test of an identical cathode using a propellant grade xenon that contained 10 ppm oxygen, intended to simulate worse case flight system impurity levels. The cathodes ran normally for the full duration of these tests'; LaB6 cathodes 'are insensitive to propellant impurities and air exposures that would normally destroy a BaO dispenser cathode'.
evidence.locator: Sec. I (pdf p. 2); Sec. II.A (pdf p. 2)
evidence.applicability: 1.5-cm LaB6 hollow cathode at high discharge current on xenon with 10 ppm O2 in the feed; the internal partial pressure is not given and the exposure is far below an air feed or air back-flow, so it neither shows nor excludes poisoning in the ABEP regime.

nodes.title: Cathode flow minimized for mass drives plume mode and energetic-ion erosion
nodes.condition: Applies only on the Xe-fed thermionic hollow-cathode branch (design_branches cathode_feed = xe_fed_thermionic).
nodes.mechanism: Lowering cathode flow to save Xe moves the cathode toward plume mode, whose instabilities generate energetic ions that erode the keeper and orifice.
nodes.physical_cause: Plume-mode instabilities at low flow and high current (S-SCOTT2024, S-SUZUKI2024).

evidence.statement: Abstract: in plume mode 'plasma instabilities generate erosive energetic ions'; onset 'occurs at even less than 2 Vpp of the keeper voltage' and 'starts at higher gas flow rates than expected from the traditional 5 Vpp metric'.
evidence.applicability: 5-75 A LaB6 hollow cathode in a vacuum chamber that simulates ion and Hall thruster operation; the abstract does not state the gas (verify from the full text).

evidence.statement: Abstract: 'The unstable plume mode of hollow cathodes should be avoided in practical applications because it severely degrades the overall cathode lifetime.'
evidence.applicability: Laboratory LaB6 hollow cathode.

decision_quantity.quantity: Plume-mode onset flow at the required discharge current vs the chosen cathode flow (plume mode erodes the keeper and orifice and shortens the cathode firing life)
decision_quantity.threshold: Spot-mode operation with a flow margin (PROPOSED; margin TBD)
decision_quantity.requires: required cathode current = maximum discharge current (design input: PPU rating)

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Demonstrate spot-mode cathode operation at the flow used in the Xe budget.

nodes.title: Air-fed cathode route: electron current or coupling insufficient at the discharge current
nodes.condition: Applies only on the air-fed plasma-cathode branch (design_branches cathode_feed = air_fed_plasma), chosen to avoid cathode Xe.
nodes.mechanism: Non-thermionic (microwave/RF) plasma cathodes on air extract less current per unit flow and power than on Xe, and cathode-plume coupling may be worse.
nodes.physical_cause: Electron energy loss to dissociation and excitation in air (hypothesis - verify); S-TISAEV2024 attributes the 30-40 % higher peak current on xenon to more effective ionisation.

evidence.statement: Air-fed microwave cathode: extracted current 'in the order of 1 A with 0.1 mg/s of air'; an applied field raises the Xe current 3.9 times but not the air current at nominal conditions.
evidence.applicability: 2.45 GHz, 24-70 W cathode on air: a magnitude (about 1 A with 0.1 mg/s of air) and a relative-to-Xe statement. The required Vyovrinda emission current is not known without Hall performance, so it neither shows nor excludes a shortfall at the required current (as for N-UTL-01, a relative or magnitude statement is context).

evidence.statement: Abstract: coupled to a 100-300 W cylindrical Hall thruster running on xenon, 'Stable thruster operation is demonstrated for the AMPCAT running on both propellants' (xenon and air at the cathode); plasma potential near the cathode was 30-40 V lower with xenon than with air.
evidence.applicability: 100-300 W class only (abstract): at the unknown required current of a < 1.5 kW Vyovrinda Hall stage it does not exclude a shortfall, so context, as the S-TISAEV2023A item.

evidence.statement: Abstract: standalone tests 'demonstrate 0.8 A of stable extracted current with 0.1 mg/s mass flow rate of a 0.48O2 + 0.52N2 mixture, relative bias of 80 V and input microwave power of 70 W'; with xenon 'the peak extracted current is 30-40% higher than air at equivalent inputs'.
evidence.applicability: Standalone cathode, no Hall thruster; a magnitude and a relative-to-Xe statement, context for the same reason as S-TISAEV2023A.

decision_quantity.quantity: Extracted electron current and coupling voltage of the air-fed cathode at the required discharge current and flow
decision_quantity.threshold: Extracted current >= maximum discharge current with margin, so the discharge is sustained at every operating point (PROPOSED; margin TBD)
decision_quantity.requires: maximum discharge current (design input: PPU rating)

nodes.milestone_A_condition: If an air-fed cathode is used: demonstrate its current and coupling at the required discharge current.
nodes.evidence_gap: The extracted currents reported for air-fed microwave cathodes (about 1 A order with 0.1 mg/s of air, S-TISAEV2023A and S-TISAEV2024) cannot be compared with the required emission current until the Vyovrinda discharge current is known (TBD - requires the maximum discharge current from the PPU rating and M-CATHAIR at that current).

nodes.title: Intrinsic cathode life: emitter evaporation at the required emission current ends insert life before the firing hours
nodes.condition: Applies only on the Xe-fed thermionic hollow-cathode branch (design_branches cathode_feed = xe_fed_thermionic).
nodes.mechanism: Independent of oxygen, the thermionic insert loses material by evaporation at its operating temperature; a higher required emission current density needs a hotter insert, which evaporates faster, so insert life can fall short of the firing hours.
nodes.physical_cause: Temperature-driven evaporation of the bulk LaB6 emitter (Lafferty evaporation data as used by S-GOEBEL2017), with the temperature set by the emission current density through the Richardson-Dushman relation.

evidence.statement: 'the cathode life is determined primarily by the evaporation rate of the bulk LaB6 material at typical operating temperatures'.
evidence.applicability: Secondary statement (citing the paper's ref. 12) for LaB6 hollow cathodes in general; it names the life-limiting mechanism, not a value for an ABEP cathode.

evidence.statement: Abstract: a 1-D disk evaporation model using in-situ insert temperatures, compared with a 4000-h wear test, projects that 'This 1.5 cm cathode is projected to exceed 50,000 hours of operation at the nominal 20-25 A of discharge current'.
evidence.applicability: A 1.5-cm LaB6 cathode at 20-25 A on xenon for a 12.5-kW Hall thruster; it shows the mechanism can be held beyond 15,000 h in that design, not for a cathode sized for a < 1.5 kW ABEP system, whose emission current is not yet known.

decision_quantity.quantity: Evaporation-limited insert life at the emitter temperature needed for the required emission current (I_emit from current continuity)
decision_quantity.threshold: Insert life > 15,000 h firing (RFP) with a life margin (PROPOSED; margin TBD)
decision_quantity.requires: required emission and evaporation-limited life (A-CATHODE) at the emitter temperature measured on the selected cathode at that current (M-CATHXE); a model alone uses a Richardson-Dushman temperature that has not been measured on the Vyovrinda cathode

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Show that the selected cathode's evaporation-limited insert life at the required emission current exceeds the firing hours with margin, using a measured emitter temperature.
nodes.status_note: 'supported' means the evaporation mechanism is credible (S-GOEBEL2017 names it as the life limiter of LaB6 cathodes). It does not mean the literature shows an insert life below 15,000 h: the only quantitative item, the projection beyond 50,000 h at 20-25 A for a 1.5-cm cathode, points the other way at that cathode's operating point and is context here because the Vyovrinda cathode and current differ.

nodes.title: Xe-fed cathode current range does not cover the required emission current
nodes.condition: Applies only on the Xe-fed thermionic hollow-cathode branch (design_branches cathode_feed = xe_fed_thermionic).
nodes.mechanism: The Xe-fed hollow cathode must emit the discharge current plus any keeper and interstage current at every operating point; outside its demonstrated current range it either cannot supply the emission at a life-compatible temperature (coupling to N-CAT-05) or runs in an undemonstrated regime.
nodes.physical_cause: Emission current density rises steeply with insert temperature (Richardson-Dushman; LaB6 emits over 10 A/cm2 at 1650 C per S-GOEBEL2017); the insert area fixes the current reachable at a given temperature.

evidence.statement: 'LaB6 hollow cathodes have demonstrated discharge current capabilities from 5 to 300 A'; the HERMeS cathode 'runs nominally at 7.5 to 100 A'; polycrystalline LaB6 'will emit over 10 A/cm2 at a temperature of 1650 ˚C'.
evidence.locator: Sec. I (pdf pp. 1-2); Sec. II.A (pdf p. 2)
evidence.applicability: Current ranges of a family of LaB6 cathodes and of one 1.5-cm high-power cathode; no range is given for the cathode size and current of a < 1.5 kW ABEP system, so context only.

nodes.evidence_gap: No open item read by this lane gives the demonstrated current range of a Xe-fed cathode sized for a < 1.5 kW Hall stage (TBD - requires L-CATHODE, or M-CATHXE on the selected cathode).

decision_quantity.quantity: Required emission current I_emit = I_d + I_keeper + I_interstage (I_d bounded by P_avail / V_d without a Hall closure) against the demonstrated current range of the selected cathode
decision_quantity.threshold: I_emit inside the demonstrated current range with margin at every operating point, so the discharge is sustained (PROPOSED; margin TBD)
decision_quantity.requires: required emission from A-CATHODE and the demonstrated current range of the selected cathode from M-CATHXE

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Show that the selected Xe-fed cathode has demonstrated emission over the required current range, including keeper and interstage current, with margin.

nodes.title: Restart count exceeds the thermionic cathode's heater/ignition cycle capability
nodes.condition: Applies only on the Xe-fed thermionic hollow-cathode branch (design_branches cathode_feed = xe_fed_thermionic).
nodes.mechanism: Each restart of a thermionic hollow cathode needs a heater cycle and a cathode ignition; a heater or ignition circuit with a smaller demonstrated cycle count than the restart count limits the mission.
nodes.physical_cause: Cycle-limited heater and ignition hardware (stated as the failure hypothesis; no cycle-life source was read by this lane - verify through L-CATHODE).
nodes.evidence_gap: No open item read by this lane gives the heater/ignition cycle capability of a Xe-fed cathode sized for a < 1.5 kW Hall stage (TBD - requires L-CATHODE, or heater/ignition cycling in M-CATHXE on the selected cathode).

decision_quantity.quantity: Required starts N_start (A-OPS) against the demonstrated heater/ignition cycles of the selected Xe-fed cathode
decision_quantity.threshold: Demonstrated cycles >= N_start with a cycle margin (TBD - requires the owner's restart count; margin PROPOSED)
decision_quantity.requires: A-OPS for the restart count (from owner assumptions) and the demonstrated cycle count from M-CATHXE

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Show that the selected Xe-fed cathode's demonstrated heater/ignition cycles cover the restart count with margin.

nodes.title: Air-fed plasma cathode wears out before the firing hours
nodes.condition: Applies only on the air-fed plasma-cathode branch (design_branches cathode_feed = air_fed_plasma).
nodes.mechanism: A non-thermionic cathode has no emitter to poison, but its discharge chamber, antenna/coupler and extraction orifice face an oxygen-bearing plasma for the firing hours; their wear or oxidation sets the cathode life.
nodes.physical_cause: Sputtering of plasma-facing parts by energetic air species and redeposition of oxidised sputtered material (S-TISAEV2024: an exposed Mo antenna was sputtered and an MoOx coating on internal surfaces lowered the extracted current within about 1 h; alumina isolation of the antenna removed the coating in two-hour tests). Whether any part wears out before 15,000 h is not shown by any item - verify.

evidence.statement: Exposed Mo antenna of a 2.45 GHz air-fed microwave cathode run on a 0.48O2 + 0.52N2 mixture: the dull region at the antenna tip 'suggests sputtering of the surface due to impacts of high-energy air species, which is supported by the heavily cratered surface visible in the SEM'; 'a non-conductive blue-grey coating is found to develop on the internal cathode surfaces, leading to decreasing extracted current with test duration', which 'likely originates due to Mo species sputtered from the antenna and oxidised'.
evidence.applicability: The AETHER air-fed microwave cathode (AMPCAT) with an exposed Mo antenna, about 1 h per test: sputtering of the antenna and an oxide coating that lowered the extracted current show that air-plasma wear operates in this cathode type; no rate over life-relevant hours is given.

evidence.statement: With the antenna electrically isolated by alumina, 'electrically isolating the molybdenum antenna from the plasma avoids formation of the MoOx coating on internal surfaces, allowing continuous cathode operation without a decreasing current with time'; the refined, water-cooled prototype ran 'two tests, each conducted for a duration of two hours' on the 0.48O2 + 0.52N2 mixture, which were 'deliberately terminated' and after which post-test inspections showed neither visible damage to the PTFE dielectric 'nor any noticeable coating of the plasma-interfacing surfaces'.
evidence.applicability: The mitigated design (alumina-coated antenna, laboratory water cooling of the microwave connector) ran two two-hour tests without visible coating: this shows the coating can be avoided over hours, not a life of 15,000 h, so it is context and does not contradict the node.

nodes.evidence_gap: No item reports a wear rate or life of an air-fed plasma cathode over life-relevant hours; the mitigated design was run for about 2 h per test (TBD - requires an M-CATHAIR wear run with the A-THERMAL life extrapolation).

decision_quantity.quantity: Wear- or oxidation-limited life of the air-fed cathode at the required current and air flow
decision_quantity.threshold: Cathode life > 15,000 h firing (RFP) with a life margin (PROPOSED; margin TBD)
decision_quantity.requires: wear or oxidation rate from a defined run (M-CATHAIR) and its extrapolation to the firing hours (A-THERMAL)

nodes.milestone_A_condition: If an air-fed cathode is used: show its wear-limited life at the required current exceeds the firing hours with margin.
nodes.status_note: 'supported' means an air-plasma wear mechanism was observed in this cathode type (exposed antenna, about 1 h); it does not mean the literature shows a life below 15,000 h: the mitigated design ran two-hour tests without visible coating, and no item gives a life-relevant rate.

nodes.title: Restart count exceeds the air-fed plasma cathode's ignition cycle capability
nodes.condition: Applies only on the air-fed plasma-cathode branch (design_branches cathode_feed = air_fed_plasma).
nodes.mechanism: Each restart needs an ignition of the air-fed plasma cathode (microwave or RF breakdown on air); a smaller demonstrated ignition count than the restart count limits the mission.
nodes.physical_cause: Ignition reliability and cycle-limited ignition hardware (stated as the failure hypothesis; no source read by this lane - verify).
nodes.evidence_gap: No open item read by this lane gives ignition cycle data for an air-fed plasma cathode (TBD - requires L-CATHODE, or ignition cycling in M-CATHAIR).

decision_quantity.quantity: Required starts N_start (A-OPS) against the demonstrated ignition cycles of the selected air-fed cathode
decision_quantity.threshold: Demonstrated cycles >= N_start with a cycle margin (TBD - requires the owner's restart count; margin PROPOSED)
decision_quantity.requires: A-OPS for the restart count (from owner assumptions) and the demonstrated ignition count from M-CATHAIR

nodes.milestone_A_condition: If an air-fed cathode is used: show its demonstrated ignition cycles cover the restart count with margin.

nodes.title: Hall magnetic circuit (coils or permanent magnets) exceeds its temperature limit
nodes.mechanism: Discharge losses deposited on the walls flow into the magnetic circuit; magnets and coils lose field or insulation above their limit.
nodes.physical_cause: Wall heat flux conducted to the magnetic circuit, named as the usual Hall-thruster thermal limit by S-SIMMONDS2022 and S-MYERS2016 (neither states a gas). Whether molecular propellants deposit a larger fraction of the discharge power on the walls than xenon is not shown by the items cited here - verify.

evidence.statement: 'Limitations on increasing the plasma density and induced field are usually due to thermal management in Hall thrusters, as the heat from the electrons colliding with the channel wall flows to the magnetic circuit and thruster coils/permanent magnet, the latter of which typically have maximum temperatures of ~400 C.'
evidence.applicability: General statement without a primary citation that does not state a gas (propellant-agnostic), so it is context on this air-specific node; the limit for Vyovrinda parts comes from their datasheets.

evidence.statement: Abstract: 'The life of Hall Effect thrusters are primarily limited by plasma erosion and thermal related failures'; 'thruster operational parameters can push some components/materials beyond their temperature limits'; 'a comprehensive thermal design strategy was employed to reduce temperatures of critical thruster components (primarily the magnet coils and the discharge channel)'.
evidence.applicability: Thermal model of a Hall thruster developed by NASA GRC with JPL, correlated with test data. The abstract, the only part read, names the magnet coils (and the discharge channel) as the critical thermal components but gives no temperature and states neither the thruster nor the propellant (verify from the full text), so it is context on this air-specific node.

evidence.statement: The RIT-10 EBB was water-cooled 'as higher power consumption and higher temperatures were expected for atmospheric propellants'.
evidence.applicability: Designers' expectation for an RF ion thruster.

evidence.statement: PPS1350-TSD on pure N2: 'For the long-firing test, the operating point has been chosen at 305 V and 3 A discharge current to get the most favorable power-to-thrust ratio and to limit the discharge power to approximately 1 kW, avoiding thruster overheating for larger powers.'
evidence.applicability: Pure N2 on a laboratory Hall thruster run with a 1.4 kW power limit: the authors kept the N2 discharge power near 1 kW to avoid overheating. It is a test-planning judgement that names no component and reports no temperature, so it does not show which part (magnetic circuit, walls, anode) limits; context for the component-specific thermal nodes.

decision_quantity.quantity: Peak magnet/coil temperature at the worst-case operating point (air and Xe setpoints)
decision_quantity.threshold: Below the component limit (TBD - datasheet) with margin (PROPOSED)
decision_quantity.requires: flight temperatures from the thermal network (A-THERMAL) correlated with the thermal balance test (M-THERMAL), because a chamber does not reproduce the orbital thermal environment; component or material limits from datasheets (design input)

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Show magnet/coil temperatures below their limits at the worst-case air and Xe setpoints.
nodes.evidence_gap: No item that states the gas shows a Hall magnetic circuit reaching its temperature limit on air or N2/O2. S-SIMMONDS2022 and S-MYERS2016 name the magnetic circuit (coils, magnets) as the usual thermal limit but state no gas; S-CIFALI2011 kept the N2 discharge power near 1 kW to avoid thruster overheating without naming the component (TBD - requires L-THERMAL, or A-THERMAL with M-THERMAL).

nodes.title: RF coil/antenna, matching network or discharge tube overheats
nodes.mechanism: Ohmic loss in the antenna and matching network and RF power not absorbed by the plasma become heat at the source.
nodes.physical_cause: Antenna resistance and coupling efficiency (hypothesis; no RF coil loss or temperature source was read by this lane - verify through L-THERMAL, e.g. S-DOBKEVICIUS2016).

evidence.statement: The resonant birdcage antenna is chosen to 'Minimize power losses by providing electrically optimized antenna operating at resonance condition'.
evidence.applicability: Design intent.

nodes.evidence_gap: RF coil loss and thermal data (e.g. S-DOBKEVICIUS2016) not read in this lane.

decision_quantity.threshold: Below material limits (TBD) with margin
decision_quantity.requires: flight temperatures from the thermal network (A-THERMAL) correlated with the thermal balance test (M-THERMAL), because a chamber does not reproduce the orbital thermal environment; component or material limits from datasheets (design input)

nodes.milestone_A_condition: Show RF coil, coupler and tube temperatures below limits at the design RF power.

nodes.title: ECR magnets lose remanence or the resonator/coupler overheats
nodes.mechanism: Heat from the discharge and microwave losses raises magnet and resonator temperatures; magnets lose field (moving the resonance) and resonators detune or fail.
nodes.physical_cause: Plasma heat load and resonator or coupler losses near permanent magnets (resonator heating is named as an engineering limit by S-STASTNY2026, abstract only, gas not stated; a microwave connector overheated in an air-fed microwave cathode, S-TISAEV2024). Magnet remanence loss is not shown by a cited item - verify.

evidence.statement: Abstract: the findings identify 'the engineering limits imposed by resonator heating'.
evidence.applicability: ECR ABEP source with a MHz-range birdcage resonator. The abstract does not state the gas; the node is not air-specific (resonator heating at the design power).

evidence.statement: 'High-energy product samarium cobalt magnets are capable of generating up to 2.8 kG near the magnets surface. This puts the practical limit on the operating frequency of around 6 GHz.'
evidence.locator: Section 'Basic Design and Discharge Performance Implications' (pdf p. 8)
evidence.applicability: Magnet capability, not temperature.

evidence.statement: 'A key limiting factor on cathode operation is excessive heating of the PTFE dielectric used in the off-the-shelf microwave connector. This was found to soften and deform at temperatures exceeding ~150 °C, as measured by a thermo-couple on the connector housing ..., leading to reduced microwave transmission'; water cooling was then implemented.
evidence.applicability: 2.45 GHz air-fed microwave cathode on a 0.48O2 + 0.52N2 mixture, no applied field (not an ECR stage): the microwave coupling hardware overheated and limited operation until laboratory water cooling was added. It shows microwave-coupler overheating limiting a microwave plasma source, not the temperature of ECR magnets.

nodes.mechanism: Discharge power deposited on the channel walls and the anode raises their temperature; above the material or joint limit the wall or anode can crack, deform or degrade.
nodes.physical_cause: Wall and anode heat flux from the discharge (S-MYERS2016 names the discharge channel as a critical thermal component; S-CIFALI2011 limited the N2 discharge power to avoid overheating). The fraction of discharge power lost to the walls on N2/O2 at the Vyovrinda operating point is not established by a cited item - verify.

evidence.statement: Abstract: 'The life of Hall Effect thrusters are primarily limited by plasma erosion and thermal related failures'; 'thruster operational parameters can push some components/materials beyond their temperature limits'; 'a comprehensive thermal design strategy was employed to reduce temperatures of critical thruster components (primarily the magnet coils and the discharge channel)'.
evidence.applicability: Thermal model of a Hall thruster developed by NASA GRC with JPL, correlated with test data. The abstract names the discharge channel (and the magnet coils) as critical thermal components but gives no temperature and states neither the thruster nor the propellant (verify from the full text), so it is context on this air-specific node, as on N-THM-01.

evidence.statement: PPS1350-TSD on pure N2: 'For the long-firing test, the operating point has been chosen at 305 V and 3 A discharge current to get the most favorable power-to-thrust ratio and to limit the discharge power to approximately 1 kW, avoiding thruster overheating for larger powers.'
evidence.applicability: Pure N2 on a laboratory Hall thruster run with a 1.4 kW power limit: the authors kept the N2 discharge power near 1 kW to avoid overheating. It is a test-planning judgement that names no component and reports no temperature, so it does not show which part (magnetic circuit, walls, anode) limits; context for the component-specific thermal nodes.

nodes.evidence_gap: No open-literature item giving Hall channel-wall or anode temperatures on air or N2/O2 was located. S-CIFALI2011 kept the N2 discharge power near 1 kW to avoid overheating without naming the component; S-MYERS2016 names the discharge channel as a critical thermal component but states no gas (TBD - requires L-THERMAL / L-WALL, or A-THERMAL with M-THERMAL).

decision_quantity.quantity: Peak channel-wall and anode temperatures at the worst-case operating point (air and Xe setpoints)

nodes.title: Channel-wall erosion (physical and chemical) by N/O species limits firing life
nodes.mechanism: Ion sputtering plus chemical attack by oxygen species wears the channel walls; magnetic shielding is validated on xenon only.
nodes.physical_cause: Wall ion flux and energy on the delivered composition; O chemistry with ceramics (signs of oxygen operation on the ceramics, S-CIFALI2011; rates not shown).

evidence.statement: After the N2 and N2/O2 firings, 'The signs of operation with oxygen are also visible on the ceramics'.
evidence.applicability: Visual inspection after about 10-h firings; no rate.

nodes.title: Anode oxidation raises electrical resistance
nodes.mechanism: Oxygen in the feed oxidizes the anode surface; resistance rises over firing time.
nodes.physical_cause: Anode material chemistry with O/O2 (anode oxidation after N2/O2 firings, S-CIFALI2011).

evidence.statement: 'there are no signs of oxidation of surfaces exposed to or nearby to the plasma' and no degradation with time was noticed during the air campaign.
evidence.applicability: Short laboratory campaign on a quartz helicon source. It reports no oxidation, which does not address the node's main mechanism (sputtered or deposited conductive films on the window) and does not bound 15,000 h.

evidence.statement: Exposed Mo antenna of a 2.45 GHz air-fed microwave cathode run on a 0.48O2 + 0.52N2 mixture: the dull region at the antenna tip 'suggests sputtering of the surface due to impacts of high-energy air species, which is supported by the heavily cratered surface visible in the SEM'; 'a non-conductive blue-grey coating is found to develop on the internal cathode surfaces, leading to decreasing extracted current with test duration', which 'likely originates due to Mo species sputtered from the antenna and oxidised'.

ranking_rule.text: For each architecture, rank every eligible action by how many of that architecture's counted open nodes it decides, then by how many distinct hard gates those decided nodes link, then by how many counted nodes it contributes to (needed jointly with other actions), then by how many it informs, then cheapest kind first, then action id. Ties are broken only by these keys. Actions touching no counted node are omitted. The rule is applied separately to the core set (nodes that apply whatever the design branches) and to each design-branch option's own set; the core ranking never counts a branch-specific node.
ranking_rule.eligibility: An action is eligible if blocked_by is empty. Blocked actions (today only A-HALLMAP, blocked by the empty credible set and incomplete O4 dispositions) are listed separately with the nodes they touch and are not ranked. Only open nodes without sub_cause_of are counted: a sub-cause node repeats its parent's threshold comparison, so counting it would count one comparison twice. Sub-causes are listed in the trees and in n_sub_causes_not_counted.
ranking_rule.branch_rule: A node with 'branch' applies only if that design-branch option is chosen (design_branches). Options of one decision are mutually exclusive, so their nodes are alternatives, not additions: they are excluded from the core ranking (counted in n_branch_nodes_not_counted) and ranked in branch_rankings, one list per option, over that option's nodes only. An action whose 'branch' names an option may touch only nodes of that option. A conditional selection (milestone A) states the chosen options and carries the core conditions plus those of the chosen options.
ranking_rule.no_weighting: No weights, probabilities or expert scores enter the ranking. The only non-count key is the categorical cost rank literature < analysis < measurement, used as a tie-break after all counts. No option of a design branch is weighted or preferred.
